name: Low-sodium / low-carb face de-bloat

lead: People lower dietary sodium and carbohydrates, often before photos or events, to reduce water held in the face and body and get a sharper jaw and cheeks.

Medical references describe edema as fluid buildup in tissue and list sodium retention among its mechanisms, with reduced salt intake used in management when sodium retention is the cause. Swelling around the eyes is usually most noticeable right after waking and from lying flat, and typically settles after time upright. No studies found test dietary sodium or carbohydrate changes on facial appearance.

paras: It is a short-term routine of a few days: cutting salty and processed foods, lowering carbs, and drinking water, usually timed ahead of an event.
Medical references note that facial and eye-area swelling, particularly sudden or painful swelling, can reflect underlying conditions and call for clinical attention.

angle.text: Users cut salt and carbs before photos or events to drop facial water retention. Less sodium means less fluid held in tissue, so the face looks sharper and less puffy. The sodium-fluid link is documented; no study tests it for facial appearance.

lead: Low-sodium and low-carb face de-bloating refers to adjusting diet, mainly salt and carbohydrate intake, to reduce fluid retention that practitioners say blurs facial definition. It is typically a short-term practice used before photos or events.

Medical references describe edema as fluid buildup in tissue and list sodium retention among its mechanisms, with reduced salt intake used in management when sodium retention is the cause [1]. Swelling around the eyes is usually most noticeable right after waking, and facial swelling from lying flat typically resolves after time upright [1]. No studies found test dietary sodium or carbohydrate changes on facial appearance.

paras: Edema is described as an abnormal accumulation of fluid beneath the skin or in body cavities. Fluid movement is governed by hydrostatic and oncotic pressure, and raised hydrostatic pressure often reflects kidney retention of sodium and water [1]. Listed causes include heart, kidney and liver disease, medications, menstruation and pregnancy [1].

Periorbital swelling is usually most apparent on waking, possibly because fluid shifts while lying flat. Facial swelling from vein obstruction during sleep typically resolves after being upright for much of the day [1]. Sudden swelling or swelling accompanied by pain or shortness of breath is described as more concerning [1].
